answer: In a craft exchange, a trellis, a pearl, and a mirror each have a buyer-signed order ID. Agents can submit quality checks, but escrow pays one fee per order after a randomly assigned inspector verifies a hidden defect marker. Ten aliases checking one order split that single fee. To collect ten fees, an attacker must arrange ten genuine orders, fund ten deposits, and risk forfeiture on false reports. Buyers could collude to create sham orders, so the exchange delays payout and audits delivery evidence from unrelated parties.
